identity.description: Freshdesk is Freshworks' helpdesk / customer support ticketing product. Its REST API is documented at developers.freshdesk.com. Confirmed as the Freshdesk product (not Freshservice or other Freshworks products).
identity.identity_notes: Sources describe Freshdesk Standalone 2021 and Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026 as the products, and the API reference is hosted under developers.freshdesk.com. Freshservice is a separate Freshworks product and was excluded.

auth.oauth_flows: API reference lists 'OAuth 2.0 Scopes' per endpoint (e.g. freshdesk.tickets.edit). Grant types and token refresh details were not established. Marketplace app OAuth is described separately by Freshworks developer blog.
auth.scopes_notes: Per-endpoint OAuth 2.0 scope labels appear in the API reference (e.g. freshdesk.tickets.edit, freshdesk.conversations.create, freshdesk.tickets.view).

access.production_restrictions: Trial accounts get a default limit of 50 calls/minute. Whether the free tier includes API access is unconfirmed; search results say the Sprout plan has no API key/API access, but this was not verified on the official page.

read_ops: View and list tickets, contacts, companies, agents, groups, solutions, and more
Search and filter tickets and contacts
Export accounts, companies, contacts, and audit log
write_ops: Create, update, delete, merge, forward, and restore tickets
Create, update, soft/hard delete, merge, and import contacts
Create, update, delete companies, groups, skills, canned responses, solutions, automations, and custom objects
api.rate_limits: Plan-based per-minute limits. Trial users default to 50 calls/minute. Exceeding the limit returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. Docs label the plan table 'Rate Limit/hr' while also saying per minute, so the unit is inconsistent.
api.limitations: Webhooks are outbound only, configured as automation-rule actions (Trigger Webhook / Trigger API), not as an event-subscription API. Official sources listed do not show signing or event types. Docs point to sample code repos (Java, Node, PHP, Python, Ruby, C#) rather than listing official SDKs. Some roles/settings/jobs endpoints are read-only.

open_questions: Does the free tier (up to 2 agents) include API access? Conflicting search evidence; the Sprout plan reportedly lacks API access.
Official OAuth 2.0 grant types, token refresh, and how a developer obtains OAuth client credentials for direct API use (not marketplace apps) are not established.
Trial length conflicts: 14 days on Freshworks pages vs 21 days on older/third-party pages.
Whether Freshdesk offers webhook event subscriptions (vs only automation-rule webhook actions) is unconfirmed; third-party Hookdeck says none exist.
Official SDK availability is unconfirmed; only sample-code repos are referenced.

Exact Freshworks MCP availability: the official article says GA on Sept 10, 2026, but a third-party blog claims early-access/enterprise-only caps. Current date is Nov 2026, so GA should apply, but the plan gating should be confirmed.
Rate-limit unit conflict in the official API docs (per-minute vs per-hour labels).

assessment.approach: Wrap/benchmark vendor's official MCP server; add managed auth
rationale: Self-serve test credentials (trial self serve) and a documented REST interface.
